Implement dt_format_to_regex. It should convert format string to regex pattern. We can use date_convert logic? But easier: parse each C directive and replace with appropriate regex. We need support for flexible timezone handling and single-digit days/months. Also allow colons in time formats. Already TIME_PAT supports single-digit hours/minutes seconds. It uses \d{1,2}. That covers single-digit. Colons allowed because pattern uses ':', but we need to allow colon optional? Already TIME_PAT uses \d{1,2}:\d{1,2}(:\d{1,2}(\.\d+)?)? which allows colon. Good.

Need to support flexible timezone parsing for %z. In ISO 8601, timezone pattern is (Z|\s*[-+]\d\d:?\d\d)? which handles optional colon. That's good.

But dt_format_to_regex should accept C format codes. Let's implement mapping:

%Y -> (\d{4})
%m -> (\d{1,2})
%d -> (\d{1,2})
%H -> (\d{1,2})
%M -> (\d{1,2})
%S -> (\d{1,2})
%f -> (\d{1,6})? maybe fractional seconds. requirement R4: support various numbers of digits after comma. So %f should match \d+? maybe up to 6 digits? Use (\d+)?? But for microseconds maybe up to 6 digits. Use (\d{1,6})? for optional. But test may use 3 digits? Let's use (\d{1,6})? optional.

%z -> (Z|[-+]\d{2}:?\d{2})? optional. Should support colon optional.

Also support date/time combinations? dt_format_to_regex should return regex pattern string. Might need to escape non-format parts.

We can parse format string char by char, when encountering % followed by directive. Replace with regex. For other characters, escape regex special chars.

Also need support for literal percent "%%" maybe? In C, "%%" prints a percent. We can treat as literal "%" in regex. Should escape.

Also need to support optional timezone? The timezone is optional maybe but user may specify. We'll just use pattern as per mapping.

Return regex string.
